ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution with low-intensity (black) pixels occupying approximately 65% of the visible surface and high-intensity (white) patches occupying roughly 35%.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant low-intensity central axial corridor and trailing edge border. Large, irregular high-intensity contiguous blobs located on the lateral regions of both the left and right lobes, featuring internal low-intensity mottling.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped depression with an estimated internal angle of 35-40 degrees; depth is approximately 12% of the total vertical fluke extent.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous irregular boundary featuring high-frequency, low-amplitude serrations (peaks and valleys) across the entire trailing edge, with increased amplitude observed on the distal thirds of each lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave sweep of the trailing edge toward the median notch; the upper boundary (leading edge) exhibits a convex upward curvature toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Small, circular low-intensity clusters distributed within the white regions. Distinct high-intensity calcified clusters (barnacles) are localized at the extreme distal tips of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Highly visible, unaligned low-intensity linear pixel disruptions. Left lobe features three main diagonal parallel lines; right lobe features an intersecting 'X' or cross-hatch pattern of linear marks.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive rake mark scarring (parallel and intersecting lines) across both ventral lobes; minor irregular tissue loss and barnacle colonization at the lobe tips.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly unique intersecting linear scar pattern on the right lobe's high-intensity region, forming a distinct pixel-level geometric cross.
